label: a demonstrative used adnominally, in front of its noun (yah kitab)
note: PARTLY STALE NOTE, corrected. It said the deixis chapter teaches yah and vah as standalone pronouns and never puts either in front of a noun. The corpus DOES print the adnominal shape -- HI-C69-verb-last has yah kitaab hai and HI-C78-pehla-paath has vah kitaab padhtaa hai -- but neither lesson introduces it, so the point was genuinely uncovered and the precise complaint is that the shape was SHOWN and never TAUGHT. HI-C91-yah-kitab teaches it, and adds the reason it matters more in Hindi than the English parallel suggests: with no article in the language, yah and vah are what a writer reaches for where English would have used the, so vah aadmi is often best read as THE man rather than THAT man.
